title: Five consecutive audits questioned school safety plan reviews

beats.text: A school can have a safety plan and still miss its annual review.

visual.sub: Two years of audits found different problems with annual plan review

beats.text: In the first audit, 5 of 21 sites lacked proof of the review.

visual.kicker: Two years of audits found different problems with annual plan review

beats.text: The next audit found the annual review missing at 12 of 20 sites.
Then 4 of 11 sites missed the March deadline.

visual.kicker: Four sites missed March 1; the next year six plans were unavailable

beats.text: The next year auditors could not obtain 6 of 14 plans.
The fiscal 2023 audit identified a late approval at Woodside Learning Center.

visual.kicker: The 2023 auditors found a late approval and no October notice

beats.text: At the audit visit, the district had not sent the October notice.

visual.kicker: The 2023 auditors found a late approval and no October notice

beats.text: The law caps an assessment at $2,000 for a willful reporting failure.

visual.label: Statutory maximum for willful reporting failure

beats.text: The auditors did not document an assessment.

visual.kicker: A $2,000 assessment required a state determination of willful reporting failure

beats.text: In fiscal 2024 the next audit marked the corrective action implemented.
Every source is linked in the case file below.

chapters.p: Two years of audits found different problems with annual plan review
chapters.b: Four sites missed March 1; the next year six plans were unavailable
chapters.o: The next audit reported that the corrective action was implemented
